source: 1968 Chevrolet Chassis Service Manual, General Information and Lubrication, p.0-12

procedures.title: Powerglide transmission: fluid check and change
steps: Every 24,000 miles (sooner for trailer towing, full loads in hot weather, mountain driving or other severe use), drain the sump through its drain plug and add fresh fluid.
Run the transmission through all ranges, then check the level as above.
Lubricate the shift linkage with water-resistant EP chassis lubricant (GM 6031M).
notes: Other fluids marked DEXRON are also acceptable.
The pan does not need to come off; there is a drain plug.
The refill quantities on this page are given only for Chevrolet, Chevelle, Chevy II and Camaro.

procedures.title: Turbo Hydra-Matic: fluid and filter
steps: Follow the Powerglide schedule except for capacity and strainer.
After checking the level, push the dipstick fully home in the fill tube.
Every 24,000 miles, drain the sump and add fresh fluid to the mark.
Every 24,000 miles, replace the sump strainer.

specs.value: approximately 7 1/2 pints U.S. measure (6 pints Imperial measure)

procedures.title: Front wheel bearings: lubricate
steps: Remove the wheel and hub to reach the bearings.
Clean all old lubricant out of bearings and hub.
Pack the tapered roller bearings with high-melting-point water-resistant wheel bearing lubricant (GM 6031M) whenever the hub is off.
Do not fill the hub cavity between the bearings or the hub caps.
Adjust the bearings per Section 3, Front Wheel Bearings--Adjust.
notes: Over-packing lets grease work out onto the brakes.
Do not use "long fibre" or "viscous" lubricant, and do not mix bearing greases.
Bad bearing adjustment causes wander, shimmy and tire wear.

procedures.title: Manual steering gear: lubricant check
steps: Every 36,000 miles check the level and add EP chassis lubricant (GM 6031M) if needed.

procedures.title: Power steering: fluid check
steps: With the system hot, check the fluid in the pump reservoir.
Fill to the full mark on the dipstick with GM Power Steering Fluid, or DEXRON ATF if that is unavailable.

procedures.title: Air conditioning: sight glass check
steps: Every 6,000 miles, after the system has run several minutes, look at the sight glass under the hood.
It should be clear; a few bubbles are normal in mild weather.
Foam or dirt means a leak: repair it at once.

procedures.title: Brake master cylinder: fluid level
steps: Every 6,000 miles, check the level and keep it 1/4" below the lowest edge of each filler opening.

specs.value: GM Hydraulic Brake Fluid Supreme No. 11
1/4" below lowest edge of each filler opening

procedures.title: Parking brake: lubricate
steps: Every 6,000 miles, apply water-resistant lubricant (GM 6031M) to the cable, the guides and all moving links and levers.

procedures.title: Clutch cross-shaft: lubricate
steps: No routine lubrication is needed.
At 36,000 miles, or earlier if needed, take out the plug, fit a grease fitting and apply EP chassis lubricant (GM 6031M).

procedures.title: Chassis lubrication
steps: Lubricate the points shown on the lubrication chart at the intervals given there (see figure 14 in the manual for Corvette).
notes: "Chassis lubricant" means water-resistant EP chassis grease meeting GM 6031M, applied with a pressure gun.

procedures.title: Hood catch and lock plate: lubricate
steps: Every 12,000 miles or 12 months, whichever is first, apply Lubriplate or equivalent to the hood catch and lock plate.

procedures.title: Body lubrication points: Corvette
steps: Lubricate these items when the opportunity arises.
Hood latch mechanism and hinges: put light engine oil on the pivots; do not oil the lock pins or catch plates.
Rear compartment lid release and hinges: use light engine oil.
notes: Body lubrication for other models is in the Body Service Manual.
